[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Route (Old French rute, from Latin rupta via) = broken way; Harvest (Old English hærfest) = autumn, reaping time",
    "reading": "A broken path through the reaping season; the way of gathering what has fallen",
    "languages": ["en", "fr", "la", "ang"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary; Lewis & Short Latin Dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.8
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Route + 91 → 'rou-te' + 'nine-one' → 'root' + 'nein' (German no) + 'won' (past of win)",
    "reading": "The root says no, yet the harvest is won; negation turned to gain",
    "languages": ["en", "de"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Route (fr. route) = road; Harvest (fr. récolte) but 'harvest' sounds like 'har-vest' → 'her' (she) + 'vest' (garment)",
    "reading": "Her garment on the road; the feminine cloak of the gathered grain",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Route 91 Harvest → 'Aster' + 'vour' + 'the' + '91' → 'Aster' (star) + 'vour' (from devour) + 'the' + 'one'",
    "reading": "The star devours the one; the celestial reaper consumes the singular",
    "languages": ["en", "grc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "R (res) + 9 (novem) + 1 (unum) + H (harvest) → R + N + U + H → 'Renu' (renew) + 'h' (heh, breath)",
    "reading": "Renewal through breath; the nine and one become a new beginning in the field",
    "languages": ["la", "he"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "R = road (via), 9 = completion (novem), 1 = unity (unum), H = heh (window, breath), V = vav (hook, nail)",
    "reading": "Road of completion and unity, window and nail; the path is nailed open to the sky",
    "languages": ["la", "he"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "Route (R=18, O=15, U=21, T=20, E=5) = 79; 91 + 79 = 170; Harvest (H=8, A=1, R=18, V=22, E=5, S=19, T=20) = 93; 170 + 93 = 263",
    "reading": "263 reduces to 2+6+3=11, the master number; the road and harvest sum to illumination",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Harvest from Proto-Germanic *harbistaz, related to Old Norse haust, meaning 'to pluck' or 'to tear off'",
    "reading": "The tearing off of the ripe; the violent beauty of the autumnal gathering",
    "languages": ["en", "non", "gem"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary; Kroonen, Etymological Dictionary of Proto-Germanic",
    "confidence": 0.7
  }
]
